- tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py:test_provider_egress_tool_is_rejected_by_host_broker (@pytest.mark.parametrize("tool_type", ...)) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The parametrized provider-egress test omits the bash/text-editor code-execution tool types that the relay’s denylist misses.
  WHY: The test gap leaves the missed provider-executed tool families uncovered by CI, and the companion `test_provider_egress_predicate` mirrors the omission.
- changelog.d/6494-claude-sandbox-egress-lockdown.md:3 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The changelog claims the relay rejects code-execution tools even though the implementation does not reject the cited bash/text-editor code-execution types.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py:49, 103 | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The host relay uses a prefix-based denylist for provider-side tool types, so tool types outside the listed prefixes can pass the check and be forwarded upstream with the pool OAuth bearer.
  WHY: The relay is the last host-side trust boundary before the Anthropic API; an allowlist of safe client-executed tool types would not rely on the denylist staying current with provider-side tool types Anthropic introduces.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py: request_has_provider_egress function (lines 86-110) | PROBLEM: The relay uses a blocklist-based approach for provider-executed tools that may be bypassed by new tool types outside the current prefix/type logic. WHY: The approach may be susceptible to bypasses if new tool types are introduced. Suggested minimal fix: transition to an allowlist-based approach for allowed provider-side tools, if such allowlist exists.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py: PROVIDER_EGRESS_TOOL_PREFIXES (line 49); tool-type branch in request_has_provider_egress (lines 101-104) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The provider-egress denylist matches provider-side tool types only by prefix, so `bash_code_execution_20250825` and `text_editor_code_execution_20250728` without any of the listed top-level keys are forwarded upstream with the broker's OAuth bearer.
  WHY: These tool types execute code on Anthropic's infrastructure with network access to Anthropic's services, bypassing the container's `--network none` isolation; the parametrized test only exercises `code_execution_20250522`, which starts with the listed prefix.
- tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py: test_provider_egress_tool_is_rejected_by_host_broker (the @pytest.mark.parametrize("tool_type", ...) block) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The parametrized provider-egress test omits `bash_code_execution_20250825` and `text_editor_code_execution_20250728`.
  WHY: The relay’s missing-prefix coverage is invisible to CI, and the companion `test_provider_egress_predicate` mirrors the same omission.
- changelog.d/6494-claude-sandbox-egress-lockdown.md: line 3 — "the host provider relay rejects server-side web, code-execution and MCP connectors" | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fragment claims the relay rejects "code-execution" tools although it only rejects tool types whose string starts with `code_execution_`.
  WHY: Operators reading the changelog may assume the cited provider-executed code-execution types are blocked; the `agents.md` note ("rejects requests that declare provider-side web, code-execution or MCP-connector tools") also overstates what the relay enforces today.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION | scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py: PROVIDER_EGRESS_TOOL_PREFIXES tuple
  PROBLEM: Prefix-only matching misses provider-side code-execution types whose `code_execution_` is not at the start of the type string.
  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: extend the prefix list with `bash_code_execution_` and `text_editor_code_execution_`, and add the two missing types to the `@pytest.mark.parametrize` tool_type list in tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION | scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py: request_has_provider_egress tool-type branch
  PROBLEM: A non-string or list-typed `type` field is treated as "has provider egress" (returns True), but an entirely missing `type` is treated as "client tool".
  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: keep current behaviour; consider replacing the startswith check with a `("web_search_", "web_fetch_", "_code_execution_")` suffix/prefix tuple so future Anthropic variants (e.g. `python_code_execution_*`) are caught without a code edit, plus a single `re.compile(r"^(web_search_|web_fetch_|_code_execution_)")` test.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py:49-50, 101-104 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The relay rejects only tool types matching `web_search_`, `web_fetch_`, or `code_execution_`, plus the exact type `mcp_toolset`; provider-side types such as `bash_code_execution_20250825` and `text_editor_code_execution_20250728` pass this check.
  WHY: A request containing either type is forwarded by the broker with its OAuth bearer, allowing provider-side code execution to bypass the sandbox’s network restriction.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

  PROBLEM: The denylist does not block provider-executed code execution types such as `bash_code_execution_20250825` and `text_editor_code_execution_20250728`.
  WHY: `request_has_provider_egress` returns False for these types, and the request is forwarded upstream with the broker's OAuth bearer; provider-executed tools run on Anthropic's infrastructure and can exfiltrate data through the provider's response.
